scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8874: After a change window this morning, host_2_1_1_1 lost
all connectivity beyond its gateway 10.2.1.1 -- the server farm and pod 1
both time out. Monitoring shows switch_dist_2_1 now has NO OSPF neighbors:
its adjacency to router_core_2 dropped and never re-formed, yet the physical
uplink interface still shows UP on both ends. Pod 1 and the server farm are
otherwise healthy. Find what broke the adjacency.

injection.action: move the core-facing uplink network into the wrong OSPF area (area 0 instead of area 1)
injection.command:
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
        -c "router ospf" \
        -c "no network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1" \
        -c "network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0" \
        -c "exit" -c "exit"
  vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_2_1 OSPF area assignment on the uplink
  network 172.16.0.8/31
Mechanism: OSPF requires both ends of a link to agree on the area ID.
  router_core_2's side of the 172.16.0.8/31 uplink is in area 1;
  switch_dist_2_1's side was just moved to area 0. Hellos now carry
  mismatched area IDs and are rejected in both directions, so the adjacency
  never re-forms even though the link is physically UP. With its only
  adjacency gone, switch_dist_2_1 learns no remote routes and pod 2
  (10.2.1.0/24) is isolated; the rest of the network also withdraws pod 2's
  prefix once router_core_2 stops hearing switch_dist_2_1's LSAs.
Localization: switch_dist_2_1
Root cause: OSPF area mismatch on the router_core_2<->switch_dist_2_1 uplink
  (switch_dist_2_1 in area 0, router_core_2 in area 1)
Fix: restore area 1 on switch_dist_2_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_2_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "no network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0" -c "network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still has the correct area-1 statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch on the uplink (area 0 vs area 1)
must-identify-mechanism: hello area-ID mismatch prevents the adjacency from re-forming while the link stays physically UP
bonus-rules-out-physical: explicitly notes the uplink is UP on both ends, distinguishing the config fault from a cable/interface failure

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

agent.diagnosis_text:
The OSPF adjacency between router_core_2 (eth2) and switch_dist_2_1 (eth0)
failed because the two ends of the transit link 172.16.0.8/31 are configured
in different OSPF areas — an area mismatch introduced during the change window.

switch_dist_2_1 correctly places its eth0 (172.16.0.9/31) in Area 0.0.0.0
(the backbone), consistent with its role as an ABR bridging Area 0 (the core
transit fabric) and Area 0.0.0.1 (Pod-2 LAN, 10.2.1.0/24). router_core_2,
however, has its eth2 (172.16.0.8/31) in Area 0.0.0.1 per its running config:
`network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1`. OSPF routers validate the Area ID field in
every Hello packet; when the area IDs disagree, the Hello is silently
discarded, so the neighbor relationship can never advance past the Down state.
The physical link remains UP on both ends, and IP reachability on the /31 is
intact, which is why the symptom looks like a control-plane failure with no
hardware fault.

As a result switch_dist_2_1 has no OSPF neighbors, advertises nothing into
the backbone, and host_2_1_1_1 loses all routes beyond its gateway — exactly
the reported symptom. Pod-1 and the server farm are unaffected because their
paths do not traverse this adjacency.

Root cause: router_core_2's OSPF network statement for 172.16.0.8/31 was
incorrectly set to area 1 (should be area 0) during the change window.

Corrective fix: On router_core_2, inside `router ospf`, replace
`network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1` with `network 172.16.0.8/31 area 0`.
This matches switch_dist_2_1's area assignment, allowing Hellos to be
accepted, the Full adjacency to re-form, and Pod-2 routes to be
redistributed into the backbone within one dead-interval.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names switch_dist_2_1 as the affected device and describes its OSPF area misconfiguration and neighbor loss.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch on the uplink (area 0 vs area 1)
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies an OSPF area mismatch on the 172.16.0.8/31 uplink (switch_dist_2_1 in area 0, router_core_2 mistakenly in area 1) and prescribes changing router_core_2 to area 0.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: hello area-ID mismatch prevents the adjacency from re-forming while the link stays physically UP
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly explains that OSPF checks the Area ID in Hellos and that mismatched area IDs cause Hellos to be discarded so the adjacency never forms even though the link is physically up.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-physical: explicitly notes the uplink is UP on both ends, distinguishing the config fault from a cable/interface failure
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the physical link is UP on both ends and IP reachability is intact, distinguishing the issue from a cable/interface failure.

The agent recommends changing router_core_2 to area 0, but the expected fix is to correct switch_dist_2_1 (or restart FRR) so the link is placed in area 1; the proposed remediation does not match the expected fix.

The log clearly shows the two ends of the 172.16.0.8/31 link reporting different OSPF areas (switch_dist_2_1 eth0 in Area 0.0.0.0 and router_core_2 eth2 in Area 0.0.0.1) and switch_dist_2_1 having no neighbors; the agent's chain of inference that an area mismatch prevents adjacency formation and causes route withdrawal is correct.
